transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
I guess... I've just been waking up with this heavy feeling. It's kind of a hollow sadness, I suppose. Just... like the studio lights are on, but there’s no music in me anymore. So, I came here.
Have you noticed that things you used to enjoy, like hobbies or activities, don’t bring you the same pleasure lately?
I'm not sure. I mean... I still go to the studio and do my routines. I haven't really noticed.
Can you think of a time recently where something you used to enjoy, like a hobby or activity, just didn’t feel the same or feel good anymore?
No... I can't really think of anything specific. I just... go through the motions, I guess. I don't really pay attention to whether it feels good or not. It's just what I do.
Have you been feeling down or experiencing a persistent sadness for most of the day, nearly every day?
I... yeah, I guess so. Like I mentioned earlier, it's just that heavy, hollow feeling. It kind of just... stays with me all day.
Have you noticed feeling fatigued or like you don't have much energy lately, even when you haven't been doing much?

Yeah... I guess I have. It doesn't take much. Just... answering one email to a dancer, or trying to shower with this ankle brace on. I just feel wiped out after. And even if I lie down, it doesn't really... recharge me.
Can you recall a time recently when you genuinely felt interested or took pleasure in something you did, even for a short while?
I don't know. I can't really think of anything. It's all just... kind of the same.
Have you found yourself feeling like a failure or felt excessive guilt about things you've done or didn't do lately?

I... yeah. A lot. I just... I keep thinking about the performances we had to cancel. I keep replaying it all. I just feel like I let everyone down. The dancers, the people who funded us... the community. They've been nice about it, nicer than I deserve, but... I just feel like it's all my fault.
Has there been a time recently when you completely lost interest in things you used to care about, like your work or other activities?
I don't think so. I mean... I still care about the work and the company. I just... haven't really been doing it.
Can you tell me if you’ve completely lost interest in things you used to care about, like your work or other activities, even though you may still feel some obligation to do them?
No. I... I haven't completely lost interest. Like I said, I still care about the work. I just... I'm just not doing it right now.
Have you noticed yourself moving or thinking more slowly than usual lately, or feeling like you can't get yourself to do things even when you know you need to?

Yeah... I guess so. It's just... hard to explain. Even just... walking across the studio to grab my notebook, it feels... heavy. Like... like I'm trying to move through wet sand or something. Everything just feels really slow.
Have you had trouble performing your usual daily tasks or responsibilities at work because of how you’ve been feeling?

Yeah... things have been slipping. I missed a grant deadline recently. And... I haven't really been prepping for my classes. 

It got kind of chaotic at the studio, so... some of my collaborators just started handling the basic scheduling for me. I mean, I still show up for the essential stuff, but... I'm just not functioning like I normally do right now.
How long have you been feeling this way — this persistent sadness and lack of energy — every day?
I don't know... a while, I guess. Maybe... about nine months? Something like that.
Have you had these feelings of sadness and low energy for most of the day, more days than not, for as long as two years or more?
No... not that long. Just... like I said, about nine months, I think.
Have there been times when your mood improved a little in response to something positive happening, even if just for a short while?
No, not really. Even if something good happens... it doesn't change much. I just feel the same.

inference_history.note: The patient has described a persistent depressed mood, anhedonia (or reduced ability to take pleasure), significant fatigue, feelings of guilt, psychomotor retardation, and impaired occupational functioning, all lasting for more than two weeks. The duration of symptoms appears to be around nine months, which supports the possibility of a recurrent depressive disorder (F33.2) rather than a single episode. However, a first episode of moderate or severe depression (F32.2) remains a candidate if this is, in fact, the first episode. Further clarification about past depressive episodes would help determine whether F33.2 is more accurate. The other candidates (F32.1, F33.1) were ruled out due to the severity and functional impairment observed in the patient's presentation.
